title: Compose selected-child returns with local invocation frames
body:
PR2534's completed selected-child wrapper checks the root parking floor and all registered work tapes, so it cannot return while a parent still has parked data or a live foreign tape. This adds a local invocation-frame contract with a conditional proof for every finite sequential call tree. The predecessor's flat-scope result remains valid.

The wrapper protects both ancestor parking and its own parked packets, transfers ownership through nested returns, and adds exactly `12(W+S)` charged moves and `2W+3S` reads/writes/erases per invocation, excluding the callee. These costs add over the call tree. The retained actual selected f=2 Compact leaf runs inside three callers, forward/inverse, on all 4,096 records; eight selected wrappers preserve dirty state and match the independent exact oracle. Eight controls distinguish return/ownership failures from raw Python access outside the stated premise.

Native CPython 3.12.7 registered replay and Git-free source/receipt controls pass; native 3.14.5 optimized primary gives the same receipt. Separate-agent review passed the primary plus 128 sequential-two-child cases and 384 tariff checks. Sources are authenticated and compiled directly from pinned bytes. Main remains `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`; predecessor PR2534 remains `f961dcb12061c3959058aed883f48b55f365eb80` at the 14:57Z pre-submission refresh. Cached Discussion evidence is timestamped and may miss newer claims.

This is a caller composition result under completed-callee/access premises. It does not construct a numerical nonleaf C supplier, fixed-tape allocator/controller, whole-supplier hosting, 73-axis payload, all-size precision theorem or new kappa. No rollback or hostile-code isolation is claimed. Retained PR2250/2287/2483/2534 code and credit are unchanged; substantial OpenAI Codex assistance and separate AI review are disclosed.

Reproduce: `python3.12 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/selected-invocation-frames`.

Canonical investigation: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2534#issuecomment-6194592793
